what_it_does: AI inference often uses floating-point arithmetic (numbers with decimal points) to maintain precision, but this usually costs more power and area than using simpler integer arithmetic. This design is a compute-in-memory block—a chip piece that does math directly inside memory instead of moving data back and forth to separate compute units—optimized for floating-point inference on AI models. The key innovations are: (1) a broadcast-alignment scheme that handles the messy alignment operations that normally don't fit well with how memory naturally processes data in parallel, (2) a custom multiply-accumulate unit that uses a non-standard number format to reduce wasted energy on sign bits and negative numbers that don't actually occur in sparse networks, and (3) support for mixed formats so the same block can run both 16-bit brain float (a compressed floating-point format) and 8-bit integer computations.
